d: The sex-determining region of the Y chromosome; it encodes testis-determining factor, a transcription factor that turns the supporting cells of the indifferent gonad into Sertoli cells.
A glycoprotein secreted by fetal Sertoli cells that makes the paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct on its own side regress; its absence or a receptor defect causes persistent Müllerian duct syndrome.
A cyst in the lateral wall of the vagina formed from a remnant of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct, which normally regresses in females.
The mesenchymal cord from the lower pole of the gonad to the labioscrotal swelling; it guides testicular descent in males and becomes the ovarian and round ligaments in females.
The pouch of peritoneum that precedes the testis through the inguinal canal; its distal part becomes the tunica vaginalis, and failure to close causes an indirect hernia or communicating hydrocele.
Müllerian agenesis in a 46,XX patient: normal ovaries, breasts and pubic hair with an absent uterus and upper vagina, causing primary amenorrhea; renal anomalies are common.
A transcription factor that SRY switches on in the supporting cells of the gonad; it makes them Sertoli cells and drives AMH, and its loss causes 46,XY sex reversal with campomelic dysplasia.

Insulin-like factor 3, a hormone from fetal Leydig cells that swells the gubernaculum and holds the testis near the deep inguinal ring in the transabdominal phase of descent; its loss can leave the testis undescended.
